Our Spurs side to take on Liverpool 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/X4f3F0cl4f

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

#1868. Liverpool: Andoni Iraola predicts how Manchester United will change under Mauricio Pochettino

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola expects a much tougher test from Manchester United following the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino.

It has been all change for today's visitors to Anfield with Michael Carrick sacked and Pochettino hired, though the Argentine only arrived on Wednesday and did not oversee training until Thursday.

But Iraola expects the new face in the opposition dugout to have his charges firing on all cyclinders, despite limited time implementing new tactics.

Writing in his programme notes for Sunday's game, Iraola wrote: “Liverpool versus Manchester United can only ever create a sense of anticipation, no matter when and where the game is played and no matter who is involved.

“For us it is a privilege and it is one that comes with a lot of responsibility because of what this rivalry means. The eyes of the world will be on us and we should use this as a motivation.

“We want – and will almost certainly need – to be as near to our best as we can. That is the standard of this fixture.

“What people think the league table tells us in this moment is not something that we can afford to be distracted by. This is a day when this kind of thing does not matter in the same way that it might otherwise. The history of the rivalry between our two clubs tells us that.

“We should expect and prepare for the best version of United because they will definitely see this fixture as an opportunity to start showing the best of themselves, particularly under new management.

“For this reason, we have to be focused only on delivering the strongest performance that we possibly can and I can tell you that the players have been incredibly focused on this in training from the moment they returned from the international period."

Despite enduring a tumultuous few seasons, Man Utd have continued to enjoy success against Liverpool. They beat them home and away last season and have lost just one of the last seven meetings.

In the games against Manchester City and Arsenal there were times when we were close to doing this but for one reason or another we didn’t quite manage it, so we need this to change.

“That means being all in from the very start and in every single moment from then on. It also means making the most of each situation. If we can do this I have no doubt that our chances of getting the kind of result that our fans and ourselves want will only increase.

#1866. Manchester United braced for legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel: Insiders express concern for 16-year-old wonderkid's welfare amid fears of 'tapping up' by Spanish giants

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 06:43 EST, 18 November 2026

Manchester United have expressed their concern over the circumstances surrounding JJ Gabriel’s imminent move to Real Madrid, and threatened legal action if there is any evidence that he was induced to leave.

The 16-year-old winger posted a video on social media on Tuesday night confirming his departure from United as talks with Madrid continue between his new agent Ali Barat and close family at the club’s Valdebebas headquarters.

United sources say they are disappointed the video appeared without any contact with them, but the club will maintain its policy of not punishing Gabriel for what it sees as the actions of adults.

However, they have reiterated that United will fight with every legal means possible if any evidence of inducement from another club comes to light.

It’s understood that United have been unable to make contact with Gabriel – who has not been seen at the club since September – or his family despite numerous attempts to check on his welfare. They want an opportunity to ensure that he has a say in what could be a life-changing decision.

Gabriel has been training in Madrid and gave an interview to Marca earlier this month saying that he favoured a move to the 15-time European champions over rivals Barcelona, while expressing an ambition to win the Ballon d’Or.

Manchester United are prepared for a legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel

The youngster is on the verge of joining the Spanish giants in a controversial move

He is registered as a United player for the rest of the season and the club are refusing to tear up that agreement in the belief that he would still need approval from FIFA to make the move. However, sources stress that there has been no contact from any football authority seeking to de-register him.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football. He is registered with United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

In a farewell post on Instagram he said: 'Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

'You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

'As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered his request to leave given he had become a key part of plans in first team training sessions this season

United were left rocked in September when Gabriel's family unexpectedly requested to cancel his contract with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport revealed at the time that United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered such a move given he had become a key part of plans in first team training sessions this season under Michael Carrick.

A week later, Daily Mail Sport revealed that the decline of United since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson was the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

'His dad has ambitions for his son to be the best in the world and play with the best and learn from the best and right now that's not current situation at United - far from it,' a source explained.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under 21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Bruno Guimaraes has reacted for the first time since receiving a hostile reception on his return to Newcastle following his £75m move to Arsenal.

The Brazilian felt Newcastle in the summer, ending a four-and-a-half-year spell which saw him named captain and win the Carabao Cup.

The midfielder’s exit was somewhat acrimonious, so Saturday evening’s return to St James’ Park was greeted to boos every time he touched the ball, in what proved to be an underwhelming performance as the Gunners dropped points in a 2-2 draw.

Bruno Guimaraes is known to be an emotional character, and the reception appeared visibly affect him and was substituted by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta in the 70th minute, being replaced by Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Guimaraes later took to social media to reflect on an emotional evening and his frustration at Arsenal's failure to secure all three points.

"A different experience for me today, returning to a place where I’ve shared so many happy memories over the past five years," he posted.

"A game of two very different halves, and the frustration of not being able to take all three points at a place where it’s always tough to play.

"There's still a lot ahead of us. We keep moving forward together, always!"

Reflecting on the performance, which Standard Sport rated as the worst from an Arsenal player, Arteta said: “We spoke about that before the game because it is emotional when you have so much going on, especially in the way that he feels connected to this club, being the captain and everything that they did together.

“But I think he was very composed. He was very, very, very focused on what he had to do in the game. I think for the time that he was on the pitch, he had a very good performance.”

Emmanuel Emegha had given the home side the lead at Stamford Bridge, but it was all downhill from there for the Londoners.

Noah Okafor (2), Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson scored the goals as Leeds romped to a memorable win.

Daniel Farke’s team climbed above Alonso’s in the Premier League table thanks to the victory, with Chelsea losing five of their 11 top flight games so far this campaign.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Despite a seemingly impressive appointment over the summer, Cundy reckons Alonso will be out of work soon if that level of display is repeated.

‘We are rotten. We were so bad, it was so bad… I’m in disbelief at what I’ve just witnessed,’ Cundy said on talkSPORT.

‘That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won’t keep his job, I’m telling you that for nothing.

He added: ‘We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting. I’m still trying to find the words… as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better.

The Blues have not had a disastrous campaign so far, sitting eighth in the table, but back-to-back defeats have rung alarm bells and Alonso admits his team is showing weakness.

‘We are in a fragile moment mentally,’ said the former Real Madrid boss. ‘When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.’

‘After the equaliser, after the change (Caicedo), we lost the momentum completely,’ he said. ‘Until then, we were doing OK. ‘We need to find solutions for sure because there will be setbacks during any game and to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that it’s still so long to play, it’s something mandatory in this competition.’

#1858. Sky Sports commentator apologises to David Raya over Arsenal injury remarks

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

David Raya has been apologised to by a Sky Sports commentator, who has accused the Arsenal goalkeeper of feigning his injury.

The Spaniard was forced off during the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday night following a collision with Newcastle forward William Osula.

At first it appeared quite an innocuous incident, with Raya seemingly instigating the contact before falling to the grass. Commentator Bill Leslie suggested that the goalkeeper was exaggerating the incident.

Such a ploy has previously been seen from Arsenal and many other clubs to to give team-mates time to regroup.

But once it had become evident that Raya was in fact hurt, Leslie backtracked.

He said on Sky Sports: "David Raya does indeed look in some discomfort. Apologies if I did him a disservice there because it really didn’t look like significant contact with Osula."

Co-commentator Chris Sutton added: "Raya is holding his arm. It looks like there’s some sort of sprain.

“He is in a lot of pain. It really did look innocuous, didn’t it, the coming together."

Arsenal's medical staff treated the goalkeeper on the pitch before he was helped off, with Kepa Arrizabalaga coming on as his replacement. The incident initially raised questions over whether Raya was attempting to waste time, but it became clear he was struggling with an injury.

Similar confusion was also broadcast on BBC Radio 5 Live, with former Chelsea midfielder Pat Nevin reporting: "He is coming off. I have no idea what happened.

"It looked innocuous. It looked like David Raya knocked into the forward."

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta later confirmed Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to establish the extent of the problem.

"Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know," Arteta said.

#1854. Mauricio Pochettino has already had one wish granted as Manchester United manager

Mauricio Pochettino has already had one of his first wishes granted as Manchester United manager.

The Argentine arrived in the north west on Wednesday, immediately boarding a plane from Cincinnati after his final match in charge of the United States national team to begin work at Carrington as soon as he touched down.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach takes his new side to Anfield this afternoon to face Liverpool in a tricky first match at the helm.

The 54-year-old revealed in his introductory press conference on Friday that he wanted input in big decisions at United as his tenure wore on, and he has already had one particular request granted in his short spell in the hotseat.

In a round of quickfire questions with the club’s media team upon his arrival, Pochettino was asked whether he preferred team lineups to be formatted in shirt number or position order, with clubs having differing approaches to their pre-match graphics.

United have traditionally plumped for a shirt number-first approach, but when Pochettino’s first team selection was revealed ahead of the game against Liverpool, the Red Devils’ first XI was listed in position order.

It outlined that their new boss had gone for a classic 4-2-3-1 shape, listing Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot as full-backs, and indicating that Matheus Cunha would play up front rather than Bryan Mbeumo.

United travel to Merseyside this afternoon mired in the Premier League relegation zone, winning just once in their last 11 games.

It was a streak that lost Michael Carrick his job, with the former midfielder sacked a week and a half ago after 303 days in charge.

“I often joke with Moreira, telling him that, at the end of our careers, we should play at least one season at Partizan. I point out that I’m three years older than him, so he’ll have to make a small sacrifice so we can get back together. He’s a truly great guy.

“There’s a fantastic atmosphere in our group. It’s a real pleasure to be part of Milan.”

#1849. Chelsea stance on making shock Xabi Alonso sack decision

Xabi Alonso could be forgiven for thinking his Chelsea reign is already heading the same way as his recent predecessors following Saturday’s 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Leeds United.

The Spaniard’s appointment in the summer was seen as something of a coup given his exploits at Bayer Leverkusen, allied to the fact Liverpool and Manchester City were both seeking high-profile replacements for their outgoing managers.

A summer of significant investment saw optimism rise at Stamford Bridge and a title challenge was anticipated given the lack of a European football as a distraction.

The honeymoon period is, however, already over for the 44-year-old whose side have lost five times already and are conceding goals, 20 in 11 matches, at an alarming rate.

Despite that unconvincing record, according to Mail Sport, Chelsea will not be making any kneejerk reactions and relieving him of his duties so early in his tenure.

Chelsea have not shied away from making quick decisions on the fates of those they have entrusted with overseeing a rebuilding process in recent years, with both Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior lasting a matter of months at the helm.

Alonso is not yet under the sort of pressure that quickly became too much to handle for Potter and Rosenior, but it is fair to say he is struggling to win over an increasingly frustrated fanbase that voiced its opinion in no uncertain terms on Saturday.

Romeo Lavia, meanwhile, said Chelsea must not give in to panic after they were hammered by one of their bitterest rivals.

The home side were outclassed as Leeds ended a 27-year wait for a Premier League win in west London, with a chorus of boos ringing out at full-time.

‘Everyone is very angry and disappointed,’ said Lavia.

‘At home this is never the way you want to finish a game. We let them back in the game when we shouldn’t have. This is something we will analyse and get better at.

#1848. Manchester United hounded off pitch by own fans

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

Brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

“We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y

I think we’ve got to be a little bit careful on that one. He’s a 15-year-old boy. It’s more about the welfare and the care of JJ as a child really, or certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we’ve got to be a little bit careful of the exposure and how we jump on that.

The start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a big way.

There’s a number of things we’ll look at, we’ll dissect and I know quite a bit of where it went wrong. We can’t accept that as a group. I take responsibility, the performance towards the second half that’s on me. We’ll have to get better, we have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to get back to winning football matches.

We’ve got to keep evolving as a group. We have to keep learning and dealing with situations. Sometimes they come a bit easier than others. Tonight was a tough one. We didn’t find a way out of it. We’ve had small, little things that have gone against us in the last week or two and then it accumulates to feel that it’s a lot bigger. I think we have to be honest and say that. The late goal against Everton from outside the box. The [Manchester] City goal the other day. It can all of a sudden roll into something a bit greater but I understand the disappointment because we shouldn’t finish the game in that manner with the position we were in and we have to be humble and take that.

As United push everyone forward, Heaven is penalised for a push on Vuskovic, and that is surely that now.

Old Trafford growing impatient with how slowly United are moving the ball, a lack of options for the player in possession and they are being caught on it repeatedly by a sharp Brighton team.

United’s second-string back four looking very shaky, understandably.

Mazraoui is now back on the pitch but he does not look 100 per cent. Brighton enjoying some long passages of possession now, but you sense United are happy to drop off and let them have the ball. More promising build-up play ends with Mazraoui heading a cross over the bar for a Brighton corner.

There has been a lengthy stoppage in play while Mazraoui receives treatment for a bang on the head. United’s left-back looks a little shaken and is off the pitch now, and Mason Mount has dropped into the left-back position.

Sesko and Vuskovic are enjoying a good battle early on. Andrey Santos then sells Tielemans a little short in midfield and Brighton take advantage, but O’Riley does not have the pace to get away from Mazraoui.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf

The 19-year-old, sent off against Brighton in the FA Cup last season, has powered a left-footed shot from the edge of the box beyond Steele. That is a moment to lift the Old Trafford crowd.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge

Really slick, one-touch football from Brighton through midfield, players bumping off passes blind around the corner knowing their team-mate has read the next move, but the move breaks down at the edge of the box. #1847. Man Utd legend Gary Neville questions Mauricio Pochettino decision against Liverpool

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

Dominik Szoboszlai slammed home the resulting free kick after Yoro had denied Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, who latched onto a mistake from Matthijs de Ligt, who misjudged a ball clipped over the top.

It was two not long after as Florian Wirtz hooked home with an improvised left-footed volley after Rio Ngumoha had darted beyond Diogo Dalot as if he weren’t there down the left, dinking it into the middle for the German to slot in via the crossbar.

Substitute Victor Munoz emphatically slammed in the fourth after more superb work from Wirtz, who found the Spaniard having won the ball deep in United territory.

Pochettino could only watch on in horror as the enormity of the task he has undertaken became crystal clear to him. For now, his men sit 19th in the Premier League table, firmly mired in the relegation zone.

#1845. Leny Yoro: Why Manchester United star was sent off vs Liverpool as statement issued

Leny Yoro was sent off to mark a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United manager at Liverpool.

The Argentine head coach could only watch on in horror as his new side were thumped 4-0 at Anfield, thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

The Reds took full advantage of their visitors’ red card on eight minutes, when Yoro was penalised for hauling down Alexander Isak as the Swede sped through on goal.

It stemmed from a Matthijs de Ligt mistake, after the Dutchman, making his first Premier League appearance in over a year after a persistent back injury, misjudged the flight of a clipped ball over the top from Jeremy Jacquet.

Isak seized upon the error, Yoro failed to cover his central defensive partner in time, and the 20-year-old was forced to fell the advancing striker before he could get a shot away at Senne Lammens’ goal.

The Premier League Match Centre explained the decision to send the young French defender for an early bath with a post on its social media channels.

“The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR,” the statement read.

Referee Sam Barratt explained to his video assistant referee: “It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO.”

The VAR replied: “Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul.”

Yoro’s last-ditch challenge ultimately went punished regardless, as Szoboszlai stepped up to slam home the resulting free kick, arrowing into Lammens’ far corner to open the scoring.

The result leaves United mired in the Premier League relegation zone, in 19th place, after just one win in 12 games in all competitions.

#1844. Romano states Milan could be an option for Balde with Mendes links: “Discuss a strategy”

According to Fabrizio Romano, AC Milan could be involved in the market for Alejandro Balde once again this winter.

A central defender would be the main target for most Milan fans ahead of the winter mercato, but the possibility of signing another wing-back wouldn’t be turned down. In fact, with the left-side still proving to be a puzzling area, someone may need to be recruited.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the past, Balde has been linked and there have been several other suggestions. However, the Spaniard may be the most accessible mid-way through the season and it would seem that the Rossoneri are considering him again.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Romano looked at the left-back’s future and didn’t deny that the Diavolo could be involved for another mercato, as MilanNews relayed.

“In the last few hours, Barcelona’s sporting director Deco spoke about Alejandro Balde and said that they are not planning on Balde’s exit because we are only in mid-November; there is a month and a half to go until January.

“Barça play every two or three days and a player like Balde can clearly still be useful between now and the transfer market. It’s true that Barça has left-back cover at the moment, but Barça doesn’t want to put a player like Balde on the market publicly already in mid-November.

“The reality behind the scenes is different: Balde remains a player who could leave in January, because Jorge Mendes, the player’s agent, was in Barcelona this week to speak with the player and discuss a strategy.

“Balde could therefore leave, but we must be realistic because there are significant figures at stake, given that he earns more than €5 million net and in the summer Barcelona were asking for €50 million for him.

“We’ll see if the formula can change in January, but on the one hand, Deco says so, on the other, there’s the reality: if Balde doesn’t play as well as he hasn’t been playing between now and January, the idea of ​​Balde leaving could become concrete.

“We told you that he’s currently being offered to Roma, but the Giallorossi haven’t really picked up steam yet. They’ve also offered him to Milan; the player was initially proposed last summer, but without a transfer, nothing happened.

“We’ll see what happens with Alejandro Balde, but he’s a name for the international or possibly Italian market that we need to keep there.”

Considering Sankhoun Diawara is now being considered as a left-back, the situation is certainly not ideal. So, Milan could certainly do worse than signing Balde.

#1843. Mauricio Pochettino slams ‘unfair’ decision after Man Utd’s defeat to Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens quickly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino said in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP

‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field. We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’

Pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

‘That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card.’

Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone prior to the November international break, when Carrick was relieved of his duties.

Results over the weekend leave the Red Devils second from bottom in the Premier League with just eight points from their first 11 games of the campaign.

Liverpool, meanwhile, climb back into the Champions League places after an emphatic win over United.

Anfield boss Andoni Iraola said: ‘We have been very good away this season but at home we haven’t been good enough and still haven’t been good enough.

‘We needed a big game, and Manchester United is always a big game, to finish like this.

‘It’s true the game’s condition changes because they play with 10 most of the game, but still we’ve done our job, we controlled the game and I think it’s always nice when you can win like this in these kind of games.’

Asked for his take on the early red card, Iraola added: ‘I think he’s the last man, no? It’s a clear foul and a red card, yes?’

Manchester United and Liverpool both return to Champions League action this week, with the former travelling to Sporting and the latter visiting Club Brugge.

Jamie Carragher says he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

#1835. The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list

Joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010)

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

#1834. Mauricio Pochettino bemoans ‘unfair’ Liverpool incident in ‘painful’ Manchester United defeat

Mauricio Pochettino has called Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool “so painful”.

The Argentine, making his bow as the Red Devils’ latest head coach at Anfield, watched on as his new side were thrashed by Andoni Iraola’s hosts in a one-sided affair.

Leny Yoro was dismissed on eight minutes for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz netted the goals that handed the Reds a huge three points, and deservedly so.

Reflecting on the heavy loss, which demonstrated the sheer size of his task ahead, Pochettino bemoaned the red card as a key turning point at such an early moment in the encounter.

"So painful. So disappointed,” the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach said.

“It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after [eight] minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm. It was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical of ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy with."

The 54-year-old identified two reasons why he believed Yoro should not have been sent off, despite VAR validating referee Sam Barrott’s on-field decision to give the French defender his marching orders.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper,” Pochettino explained.

“In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

"In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

#1832. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1831. New heights and same problems: How Milan stars fared in the November international break

With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about…

Christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s quickly reminded everyone of how important he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

It gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

In terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

However, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence currently and long may it continue.

Then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

He played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

For France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

For Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

It was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

#1830. Gary Neville delivers scathing Manchester United verdict after heavy Liverpool defeat

Gary Neville believes there has been a “remarkable” drop in Manchester United’s standards after the Red Devils sank to a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday.

The club were looking to propel themselves out of the Premier League relegation zone, helped by a bounce from the arrival of new manager Mauricio Pochettino, who took charge of his first match at Anfield.

The Argentine, however, was dealt a nightmare start, as Leny Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz got the goals for Andoni Iraola’s brilliant hosts.

Pochettino bemoaned Yoro’s red card as “unfair” in his immediate post-match reaction, but he could not complain about his side’s performance on the night, as they were swept aside emphatically by their historic rivals.

On Sky Sports, former United defender Neville said that Pochettino had now seen “the worst” of his new club’s predicament.

“It's really desperate and it's tiring watching them,” he said.

“This is the worst Manchester United have ever been in 53 years.

“There's no time to work on this. Maybe this will be a good thing in the long run that Pochettino sees the worst of it.

"He's got a big job on here. There'll be an element of 'Let's just forget about this game because Yoro got sent off and it's with 10 men', but it rides into the game in midweek.

"From a defensive perspective, I've never seen anything like this.

"I grew up watching great defenders that were fantastic players that were aggressive. They were brilliant people, great fighters and had spirit.

"You watch this lot, honestly, it's unbelievable. They're going to have to advance money to [Pochettino] in January for defenders. They're probably going to need another couple next summer.

"Forget the rest of the squad for now, they've got to build from the back.

"Manchester United are the worst team in Europe defensively right now. You can't say anything more than that. It's unbelievable. 34 goals [conceded] in 15 matches.

"This is where we've got to where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as if it's just the norm and what should be accepted.

"The club standards have dropped so far, it's incredible.

"But the fans’ standards haven't dropped. They expect a Manchester United team to be competitive every single week, and what they're seeing now, Manchester United have got the worst defence in the whole of Europe, and are currently second from bottom in the Premier League.

#1829. Man City charges claim shot down as Enzo Maresca sent warning before Fulham (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 08:00

Uncertainty over Manchester City's 115 charges is without question a contributing factor to their Premier League struggles, former Sky Blues midfielder Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Enzo Maresca's side will endeavour to avoid a fourth consecutive defeat in the top flight when they host Fulham on Saturday lunchtime, having lost to Nottingham Forest, Brighton & Hove Albion and Aston Villa before the international break.

Man City's dire run of form has seen them slip six points behind Arsenal at the top of the Premier League table, while also falling below high-flying Brighton into third position, and they are just three points clear of Liverpool in fourth.

As Maresca's men try to focus on on-field matters, the appeal over their guilty verdict is a highly unwelcome distraction, and the threat of unprecedented sanctions looms if their charges are upheld.

Maresca has denied that the charges are a distraction, but Hamann - who made 71 appearances for the Citizens - has shot down the manager's claim and believes that the off-field concerns are impacting the club's performances.

"Nobody seems to know what's going to happen," Hamann said. "One person says they get off with the charges, the other says they get deducted 70 points. Everything and anything is possible. If they were to deduct 60 or 70 points, they would have to play in the Championship next season.

"I don't think many of the players, apart from maybe one or two who say they will stick it out, would want to stay. Probably 90 to 95% of the players will want to leave the club, and at some stage it has to have an effect.

"I'm a bit surprised it came so quickly after that. Maybe it's not the only reason, but it's certainly a reason they haven't played that well because they started the season really well. They played a fantastic game against Paris at home, even though they got beaten. It was the game of the season for me.

"It was absolutely thrilling and fantastic for both teams. I think it had an effect, and it may continue to have an effect. Uncertain times at City at the moment."

It has now been almost two months since the Premier League confirmed that Man City had been found guilty of all financial charges, and the verdict prompted an immediate appeal.

The appeal process must be concluded within 12 weeks, and the expectation is that the hearing will take place in mid-December ahead of a potential verdict in early January.

In the meantime, Premier League chiefs have supposedly contacted clubs to seek legal protection in case any of Man City's sponsors decide to sue; 14 clubs must approve the motion for it to pass.

Elsewhere, Man City owner Sheikh Mansour has reportedly seen a £1.5bn deal with a US investment firm collapse, thus denying City Football Group extra liquidity as the uncertainty rumbles on.

Didi Hamann was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Lottoland Live Casino.
