#1828. Andoni Iraola fires jab at Mauricio Pochettino after easy Liverpool win over Manchester United

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said his side could “celebrate at half time” during their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

The Reds ran out easy victors against their fierce rivals on Sunday, with United hoping to snap a miserable run of just one win in 12 matches.

They did not get the desired bounce from the arrival of new boss Mauricio Pochettino, who watched his side thrashed at Anfield and go down to ten men in eight minutes after Leny Yoro’s red card, which he bemoaned afterwards.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz netted the goals to hand the hosts a straightforward three points that sees them sit fourth, seven points off league leaders Arsenal.

United, meanwhile, are spiralling and remain in the Premier League relegation zone, in 19th place.

Iraola seemed to fire a jab at Pochettino and United in his post-match interview.

"It's a big win, always against United it is a big game,” he said.

“I think you can enjoy it, you can see it coming. It's difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half time and enjoy it a little bit and have lovely moments.

"We could have scored more. We missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, today we've controlled the game and everything was happening around the box.

"It's a 4-0 [win] that was good for [our confidence], trying to get better results here at home."

#1827. Newcastle Confidential: Major update on new £1.3bn super stadium as secret meeting with Wall Street money men is revealed, Amar Dedic bow and arrow case resolved and Joelinton injury boost

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026

Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a new £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.

I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular new 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.

Interestingly, the meeting came in a week when Jacobo Solis, the influential Public Investment Fund executive and club director who is rarely seen in the city, was also present. The Spaniard’s involvement is viewed as extremely significant by those close to the project, and we understand an announcement on the club’s stadium plans is now ‘very close’.

The high-level meeting with Goldman Sachs is a major indication the club's board will recommend the development of a new stadium rather than redeveloping St James’, and I understand the former is currently the preference.

There has been significant outlay on various surveys around Leazes Park in recent months. I reported in April how the presence of bats in the area was one environmental complication they had to overcome. The club has since undertaken extensive work around animal and plant life.

The alternative remains a St James’ expansion, taking the capacity to 60,000, but chief executive David Hopkinson and others among the top brass are well aware that only a new, multi-purpose home would allow Newcastle to compete financially with the world’s biggest clubs.

A secret meeting with representatives from Goldman Sachs is the strongest indication yet the club are preparing to leave St James' Park rather than redevelop it

In April, Daily Mail Sport revealed an architect’s drawing of how the new, three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated

Plans of the new stadium reveal an exterior that has been likened to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena

The proposed funding model combines borrowing, owner investment and potentially outside investors, with the debt sitting with Newcastle rather than the ownership. That makes the involvement of Goldman Sachs particularly significant as the club look to turn their ambitious plans into a financially viable reality.

Sources have described the circular design of a new stadium, and in April we revealed an architect’s drawing of how the three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated, but the exterior has been likened to both Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium by those who have seen images and video.

Club sources say they are continuing to work on options and plans for a new stadium. But the visit of Goldman Sachs – and the simultaneous presence of one of PIF's most influential figures – suggests that work behind the scenes is moving towards a decisive stage.

Having covered this story for several years, I now believe PIF will be asked to sign off on a new stadium development ahead of an announcement in early 2027.

Dedic case closed - but he's told to bow out

Amar Dedic has been given a rap on the knuckles and handed over his bow and arrows after the Newcastle defender’s ‘suspicious activity’ triggered a major police operation earlier this month.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on November 5 that the Bosnian was at the centre of a search involving at least six patrol cars after he was spotted carrying the hunting weaponry at a Northumberland beauty spot.

A concerned 999 caller, believing there could be a threat to the public, reported seeing him and a friend walking with the equipment near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the Harlow Hill area, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were intercepted in a blaze of blue lights around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic and his friend. After lengthy discussions at the roadside, police were satisfied that Dedic was using the weaponry for recreational use, but their investigation remained open.

However, I can confirm the matter is now closed and the 24-year-old has been reminded of UK law by police and the club. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in this country.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson told me: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, November 4, we received a report of suspicious activity in the Harlow Hill area.

‘It was reported that two men had been witnessed in possession of bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road. Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

'At that time, it was understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Following a number of enquiries, this has now been confirmed. The two men have since forfeited the bow and arrows and words of advice have been given to the pair. The case has now been closed.’

Dedic took the confusion in good spirit, posting a picture of Lord of the Rings character Legolas, known for his prowess with a bow and arrow, on his social media page.

Joelinton has not yet been ruled out of the Tyne-Wear derby, despite fears over a significant injury lay-off.

I revealed on November 4 that the Brazilian had suffered a fresh muscle strain and this was confirmed by Matthias Jaissle the following day. There has been a suggestion this week that the period out could extend towards Christmas, but sources have played down that possibility.

I understand Joelinton is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures. This could still be too soon for the visit of Sunderland on December 6, but the noises around the midfielder have definitely been more optimistic in the past 24 hours. The 30-year-old is expected to be the only senior absentee from the squad that takes on Arsenal this weekend.

Joelinton (left) is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures

Newcastle will NOT be signing Gambian triallists Omar Marong and Alieu Saine. I understand that, while the 16-year-olds have impressed during a two-week stay, club chiefs have decided that those already on the books are of greater potential.

Marong and Saine played in a 6-0 win over the i2i International Soccer Academy on Friday, and winger Saine chipped in with two assists. However, while there is a feeling both will secure moves to Europe in due course, Newcastle will keep a watching brief for now.

The pair are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and were identified by the club’s new global talent team. They caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals.

Neither player could have signed permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle were keen to assess their potential. It is likely that players of a similar profile from Africa will arrive on trial in the future.

Both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

Interestingly, the fourth official with whom Arteta clashed at Sunderland earlier this season will be on duty. Elliot Bell repeatedly warned Arteta not to step from his technical zone at the Stadium of Light.

When the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel

In another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

Joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

Arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

Finally, after James Trafford starred during England's 3-2 win in Spain this week, a brilliant match I was lucky enough to cover, one reader reached out to ask about an XI of players Newcastle have missed out on.

The club tried to sign Trafford on three occasions under Eddie Howe, and even as recently as this summer he appeared destined for Tyneside.

So, with thanks to the idea from Ian Spencer, here is the ‘what might have been’ XI of Newcastle targets who came close to signing…

Newcastle's What Might Have Been XI (3-5-2): James Trafford; Abdukodir Khusanov, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marc Guehi; Ivan Fresneda, Johan Manzambi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, James Maddison, Victor Munoz; Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike.

Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United reign got off to a miserable start as Liverpool punished Leny Yoro’s red card with a pair of early goals on their way to a comprehensive 4-0 win against their relegation-threatened rivals. A whirlwind week for the former Argentina international ended in all too familiar disappointment for the faltering Red Devils, whose hopes of enjoying a new manager bounce were extinguished within 13 nightmare minutes at Anfield.

Dominik Szoboszlai’s fierce free-kick Liverpool put ahead after United defender Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity and Florian Wirtz’s smart finish quickly put Pochettino’s side further behind. United temporarily stemmed the tide thanks to some last-ditch defending, wayward finishing and key Senne Lammens stops, but Andoni Iraola’s Reds redoubled their efforts in the second half.

In truth, Pochettino’s 10 men were fortunate that Liverpool only added a further two goals though Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz, such was their dominance.

There we have it. A nightmare debut for Pochettino.

Thanks for joining us on Standard Sport, be sure to come back very soon for even more live action.

86 mins: Two changes for the Reds. Gomez replaces Araujo, and Koumas is on for Isak.

82 mins: It’s four, and it’s Munoz. A lovely goal. Wirtz is instrumental once more, sliding the Spaniard in to slot home the fourth emphatically.

79 mins: Ngumoha is replaced by Frimpong.

77 mins: Huge chance! Wirtz curls in a delightful inswinger which van Dijk meets unmarked, but he can only direct wide of the target!

76 mins: Two good saves from Lammens, first to deny Isak he cuts in and lets fly, and the next from Szoboszlai.

73 mins: Here comes the young midfielder, with Victor Munoz, as Mac Allister and Barcola make way.

72 mins: Trey Nyoni is being prepared for the hosts.

66 mins: That is a scintillating counter from the hosts. Barcola bursts clear of Fernandes, leaving him in his wake, squaring for his opposite winger, who slides home the third.

#1824. Pavlovic admits he liked Conceicao despite ‘Hitler-like’ methods: “Such a circus”

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has admitted that he was a fan of Sergio Conceicao, even if his management was rather totalitarian.

It’s fair to say that Conceicao is a divisive figure within the Milan sphere. The Portuguese arrived and won the Supercoppa Italiana and there were glimpses of the Rossoneri becoming a team under him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, there were far too many incidents which turned most against him – including some members of the squad – and that gave him little hope of continuing. So, when he lost the Coppa Italia against Bologna, he was all but done, if he wasn’t before then.

He’s called it unfair since, but logically there was no way he could’ve continued.

Speaking to the Serbian podcast SS Calcio, Pavlovic admitted that he was fond of Conceicao, despite some of his strange methods, as MilanNews relays.

“Conceicao banned Nutella, and since then they haven’t allowed it [he laughs]. He was… He’s a good guy, I like him, but he had Hitler-like methods. We go away for a match and at the hotel we split up; the players stay together, everyone else stays outside.

“Knee and elbow pads are mandatory in training, whether the temperatures are below zero or 35 degrees; they have to be there.

“Three days before a match, some players went to a concert until 11 p.m.… He had assistants, or spies if you like, who reported to him, and he made such a circus out of it that in the next match, none of those five or six players were allowed on the pitch.”

Another anecdote about Conceiçao, when he had just been appointed coach of Milan…

“He was 40 minutes late to the first meeting; all the players and management were waiting for him, and he was in his office. He just wanted everyone to know who was in charge. He did it on purpose.”

It’s certainly a strong comparison to make; that’s for sure…

#1822. Monza vs Fiorentina - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 21 Nov 2026 09:32

Both battling at the wrong end of the Serie A standings, Monza and Fiorentina will vie for three precious points when matchday 12 comes to a close on Monday night.

While the hosts have slumped into the drop zone after four consecutive defeats, their Viola visitors are showing signs of revival.

Having lost six of their first eight games and recalled their former interim manager, Fiorentina had begun to steady the ship before international football intervened.

Paolo Vanoli's side have inched away from the relegation zone by claiming five points from their last three outings, with an away victory over Sassuolo being sandwiched by a pair of 2-2 home draws.

After sharing the spoils with Atalanta at the end of October, the Viola fought hard for a draw against old foes Juventus, taking the lead twice before settling for one point.

Both acceptable results in isolation, but Fiorentina's struggles at Stadio Franchi show no sign of ending: the Tuscan club's last league win on home turf dates back to April.

Now bound for Brianza, their two top-flight wins this term have both come on the road, so they will hope to pick up another on Monday.

However, sitting just two points above Monza, Fiorentina have yet to keep a clean sheet in Serie A and continue to look vulnerable at the back.

Across seven prior meetings in Monza, there have been three wins apiece, but the hosts have won two of the last three.

While precedent may suggest that they will come out on top, the Brianzoli departed for the international break on a dismal run of form.

Consecutive defeats to Torino, Napoli, Bologna and Atalanta left them stuck inside the drop zone, abruptly halting a relatively promising start.

Only Sassuolo have conceded more goals after 11 matchdays, leaving head coach Ivan Juric searching for solutions to his team's defensive woes.

Failing to score for the first time this season, the Serie B playoff winners were beaten 1-0 by La Dea last time out, continuing a grim top-flight record at Stadio Brianteo.

Dating back to their relegation campaign of 2024-25, Monza have won just three of their last 24 home games in Serie A.

Although expensive summer signing Arthur Atta is set to end a six-match absence, Fiorentina are still missing Fabiano Parisi and Marin Pongracic due to injury.

Alieu Njie returned from Sweden duty with a minor thigh problem, so Wilfried Gnonto or Pedro Goncalves could be promoted from the bench if required.

As part of an attacking trio, Njie has racked up five goal involvements from his last three Serie A appearances, while Argentine pair Mateo Pellegrino and Franco Mastantuono both have four goals this season.

Meanwhile, one man has been carrying Monza's attack: Capocannoniere leader and Liverpool target Gustavo Varela has scored more than half of their 17 league goals, netting nine in 10 games.

In the three-points-for-a-win era, only Fiorentina legend Gabriel Batistuta (13) and David Trezeguet of Juventus (10) have topped his tally for a newly promoted side after 11 matchdays.

Monza captain Matteo Pessina returned to full training during the break, having missed most of the campaign so far.

Former Fiorentina midfielder Michael Folorunsho has also recovered from a calf problem, but Yvan Maye and Jay Robinson are both doubts.

Tornqvist; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Lucchesi; Birindelli, Akinsanmiro, Foe Ondoa, Mangas; Mota, Robinson; Varela

De Gea; Jimenez, Dragusin, Viery, Mario; Ndour, Fagioli, Oulai; Mastantuono, Pellegrino, Gnonto

Fiorentina have equalled their worst defensive start to any Serie A season -  a negative record set back in 1933 - while Monza have never conceded more at this stage of a top-flight campaign.

They will surely share several goals on Monday night, but the Viola's vibrant attack should secure maximum points.

#1819. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to says he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has said the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

No questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

Ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”

“They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

5 - Alex Scott is the only midfielder in the Premier League this season to rank in the top five for times he has won possession (3rd), for the number of duels contested (=4th) and for total distance covered (5th).Sprightly. pic.twitter.com/xfVzme7JXj

Jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.

The big ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. It is understood the place of his club team-mate Eberechi Eze was also in question, but the 28-year-old has been included, partly because of the unavailability of other players. Hopefully Thomas Tuchel will explain all later.

The absence of Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White is puzzling.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the top-scoring Englishman in the Premier League since the start of last season.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN STICKS IT IN!" pic.twitter.com/UJ54wPGytV

Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the first games of the 2026-27 season, as the Three Lions begin a new Uefa Nations League campaign.

The head coach has selected a 27-man squad for the four-game window, which takes place between September 21 and October 6.

There’s a return to the Three Lions squad for a number of players following the start of the new campaign with their clubs, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Lewis Hall, Rio Ngumoha, Jarrad Branthwaite, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott all selected.

And there’s a place in the squad for Trent Alexander-Arnold, alongside his Real Madrid teammate Jude Bellingham.

Here it is! 🤩Thomas Tuchel's first #ThreeLions squad of the 2026-27 season 🦁 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

Ivan Toney likely to miss out as he is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24.

Nine weeks have passed since the agonising semi-final collapse to Argentina and Tuchel can expect a grilling about his reflections.

He will need to rebuild trust with supporters heading into a cycle that culminates with a home Euros in 2028.

Eberechi Eze could be left out of the England squad announced this morning by Thomas Tuchel ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. The Arsenal midfielder has made six appearances for his club so far this season but has only started two of those games and none in the Premier League.

The 28-year-old played four times for England during the last World Cup but Tuchel is expected to shake up his forward options. There is an expectation that there will be a recall for Chelsea’s Cole Palmer.

#1818. Tuttosport: Not just Endrick and Tresoldi – Milan eyeing Bundesliga striker Krösche admires

A new idea has emerged for AC Milan to strengthen their attack, and it is a player that incoming Head of Football Markus Krösche knows well.

This morning’s edition of Tuttosport writes that the two dreams for January are Nicolò Tresoldi and Endrick, but a third option is starting to emerge at Milan. The player is equally effective in terms of goals, but perhaps less media-burdened than Gonçalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese striker has just three goals so far for Milan since joining for a club-record €73m fee, and his current drought is now over one month. This is why finding a viable alternative in the winter is key, but perhaps without spending another €60-70m on another forward.

It will be very hard to snatch Tresoldi from Club Brugge during the winter transfer window, as Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are also strongly interested in him. Meanwhile, Endrick’s departure from Real Madrid is currently being vetoed by Jose Mourinho. So, who could the Rossoneri turn to?

Milan could look towards the Bundesliga, more specifically Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic. He is a name highly regarded by Milan’s new Head of Football – Markus Krösche – who has watched him up close for several years.

The Bosnian striker’s contract expires in 2028, and there’s currently no agreement to extend it. Therefore, his price tag – despite an  excellent start to the season – isn’t likely to skyrocket and could become affordable.

He’s already scored nine goals across all competitions: five in nine appearances in the league, and four in four in the Champions League. That seems to provide enough evidence that the Bosnia international is ready for a top club.

Ermedin Demirovic has scored a hat-trick in the first 32 minutes of Stuttgart's game with Viking.

It's the fifth earliest in Champions League history:

🇵🇱 Robert Lewandowski vs. RB Salzburg (23rd minute)🇮🇹 Marco Simone vs. Rosenborg (24th minute)🇫🇷 Kylian Mbappe vs.… pic.twitter.com/V5XA1iEwLg

— The Athletic | Football (@TheAthleticFC) September 9, 2026

Demirovic is raring to go and is eyeing potential suitors (including several English clubs). A couple of years ago, Juventus sought him as a partner to Dusan Vlahovic , when Cristiano Giuntoli was still in charge. Now, that move to Italy might finally come about.

In recent weeks, the presence of Milan scouts at Stuttgart’s matches has not gone unnoticed. Demirovic has responded in his own way: with goals. Dzeko’s heir in the Bosnian national team can also play as a second striker and therefore, if necessary, partner Ramos.

In the past he has also been used as a winger in a three-man attack. This versatility is invaluable for a chameleon-like coach like Ruben Amorim, and it would allow Ermedin to be used in any type of situation.

It would also facilitate Francesco Camarda’s possible loan exit, so this is a situation well worth watching as we reach the weeks leading up to the winter window.

#1817. Liverpool Confidential: Latest on new deals for Virgil van Dijk and Alisson as European giants circle, how Reds are trying to turbocharge academy recruitment and Joshua Abe's comeback

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which shows his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their new deals.

Alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

It was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

The Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty

Confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week

In the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

Since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Big Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a new-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Liverpool need to see more from their big-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

#1816. Harry Kane injury could force Bayern Munich into £44m transfer dilemma amid Arsenal, Man United interest

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39

Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.

The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old was withdrawn after just 20 minutes, leaving Vincent Kompany without his first-choice centre-forward at a crucial stage of the campaign. The setback is particularly concerning given Bayern's limited options in the position and their demanding domestic and European schedule.

One player who could now become increasingly relevant to the German club's recruitment discussions is Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who has been monitored by Bayern scouts in recent weeks.

However, the 22-year-old's reported valuation of up to €50m (£44m), combined with Brugge's reluctance to sanction a winter departure, presents a significant obstacle should Bayern decide to bring forward their search for attacking reinforcements.

According to German newspaper TZ, Bayern have sent scouts to Belgium on several occasions to monitor Tresoldi, whose performances have attracted considerable attention across Europe.

The Germany Under-21 international has scored 14 goals and provided one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as one of the most productive young forwards on the continent.

His form has inevitably generated transfer speculation, with reports suggesting that Bayern view him as a potential long-term addition to their attacking department.

Significantly, the club's interest emerged before Kane suffered his injury against Koln.

Earlier this month, Bayern were reportedly exploring the possibility of signing Tresoldi as an additional attacking option despite having recently extended Kane's contract until 2029. The idea was to strengthen their squad with a younger centre-forward capable of developing alongside the England international.

That strategy could now face an unexpected test.

With Kane unavailable for several months, Bayern must decide whether their existing attacking resources can compensate for his absence or whether an immediate signing would provide greater security.

Tresoldi possesses several attributes that could appeal to Kompany, including his movement inside the penalty area, ability to attack space behind defenders and increasingly reliable finishing.

However, securing his signature midway through the campaign would be far from straightforward.

Reports in Belgium have indicated that Club Brugge are determined to retain the striker until at least the summer, with the club's hierarchy reluctant to entertain offers during the January transfer window.

According to Het Nieuwsblad, Brugge have made their position clear to interested clubs, although an exceptional financial proposal could potentially force a reassessment.

German reports have placed Tresoldi's potential price between €40m (£35m) and €50m (£44m), with the forward under contract until June 2029.

Bayern have not submitted a confirmed offer, and there is currently no evidence that Kane's injury has prompted formal negotiations with the Belgian club.

Any attempt to accelerate a move for Tresoldi could also bring Bayern into competition with several Premier League clubs.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with the Club Brugge striker, whose impressive scoring record has strengthened his reputation as one of Europe's most promising young centre-forwards.

That timeline broadly aligned with Bayern's previous interest, which appeared to concern the longer-term development of their attacking squad rather than an urgent winter acquisition.

Kane's injury introduces a potentially important difference in Bayern's circumstances, although it does not establish that the Bundesliga champions have changed their transfer strategy.

The club must also assess whether investing heavily in another centre-forward would make sense once Kane returns to fitness, particularly after committing to a new long-term agreement with their leading goalscorer.

Kompany has alternatives within his squad, but none offers the same combination of finishing, creativity and experience as the England captain.

A temporary tactical adjustment may therefore be necessary, with greater responsibility potentially falling on Bayern's other attacking players.

The German champions could also turn to their academy, where 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention following impressive performances for the youth teams.

According to Kicker, the teenager was already under consideration for greater involvement with the senior squad before Kane's injury, although expecting him to replace the England international immediately would represent a considerable leap.

For Bayern, the dilemma is therefore as much about timing as identifying the right player.

Tresoldi was already an attractive prospect before Kane's setback, but Brugge's reported resistance to a January sale means that accelerating the deal could prove expensive and difficult.

Meanwhile, Arsenal and Manchester United remain interested parties whose own plans have been linked to the summer window.

Bayern's next decision will depend on whether Kompany believes his squad can absorb Kane's absence or whether the club considers an early investment necessary to protect its ambitions in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

#1815. Yoro sending-off against Liverpool ‘completely unfair’, says Pochettino

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino lamented the "completely unfair" decision to send off Leny Yoro in Manchester United's 4-0 thumping at Liverpool on Sunday.

Pochettino made a nightmare start to life as United boss, with a drubbing at the hands of their old rivals, with Yoro's eighth-minute red card setting the tone.

After Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a bouncing ball, Alexander Isak raced in on goal and Yoro clumsily brought him down outside the box, resulting in a straight red card for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

Dominik Szoboszlai netted from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz turning in an acrobatic volley to double Liverpool's lead three minutes later.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added gloss to the scoreline in the second half of a dominant display from Liverpool as United struggled to truly test Alisson until first-half stoppage time.

Pochettino insisted Yoro should not have been sent off, believing Isak was not in control at the time of the ball when the challenge happened.

"So, so painful. So disappointed," he told Sky Sports. "It's not in your head to start here in the Premier League in this situation.

"The only problem was that the game changed completely after six minutes, and now we can talk and explain everything, but the damage is done.

"It's so painful. The players are feeling the pain of this type of situation. I told them they need to be calm, and it was a completely unfair situation that happened.

"And also we need to accept to increase our concentration and also make better decisions on the field, and be much better. We need to be critical of ourselves, but also at the same time, we need to put some situations that happened during the game that we are not happy.

"The ball was going to the keeper. I think in that situation, if you review the VAR, you can see, like we see on the cameras now, that he [Leny Yoro] never had the intention to connect with [Alexander] Isak. The striker saw that the ball was going to the keeper, and he delayed a little bit of his run and goes down.

"But if you go two minutes before. Sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo, they are similar, no? When you compare the actions, that's a penalty, no?

"And if we score after six minutes, for sure we are talking in a different way. But that is sometimes one of the things where we need to take responsibility, and I am here to take responsibility and keep pushing.

"I'm not going to change what happened, and being respectful is always important. At the same time, I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card."

Mauricio and the team are grateful for your support on a difficult evening at Anfield. A big week lies ahead. https://t.co/F6kdP7gz1Z

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 22, 2026

Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club.

He also suffered the joint-heaviest defeat by a United manager in his first game, along with Lal Halditch, who suffered a 4-0 defeat in October 1926 against Bolton Wanderers in the top-flight.

Accounting for three points per win all-time, United’s eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (seven), and that tally currently leaves them 19th in the table, only one point above bottom-place Crystal Palace.

Pochettino has a mammoth task on his hands to turn things around, but he is determined to get United improving soon.

"I told the players [it was a] completely unfair situation, but when a situation is like this, to turn a negative to positive is we need to make double effort," Pochettino told BBC Sport when asked how his side responded after going 2-0 down so early.

"More concentration, more focus, care more about everything. We have players, and in a way, after the 12th minute, when we conceded and started to play with 10 men, the players were committed, and they tried everything.

"We made effort, we ran, we tried. A very difficult team, a team that found the goal when there was the red card. Every day, we will find the possibility to improve."

#1814. GdS: A red-hot start and the ‘S’ word – the data that inspires confidence in Amorim

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

It is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

To date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the new era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target announced by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

In short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

#1812. Pep Guardiola visits Bahia in new City Football Group role

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

Guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

The visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

"I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them."

Almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

During their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us."

Guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, New York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

His journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

The visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been announced, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

Nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would currently secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

For Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.

#1811. Musah lifts lid on Amorim’s faith, early career, preferred role and Scudetto ‘ambition’

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

Going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the plans for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a new destination would be found, but Amorim had other plans. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

Such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

“A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”

“I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

“I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

“I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

“It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

“Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”

“I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

“Yes, in 2021 I returned to New York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”

“Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

“Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”

You have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

“I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a plan for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

“Last year I watched them a lot; they were a very solid team and difficult to beat. Amorim brought a very positive vibe, we understand each other. He understands the player very well and vice versa.

“It helps when he understands what the players need; he’s good at that, and the players in the team are pretty calm.”

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

“Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”

“My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”

#1810. Iraola tempers title talk despite Liverpool’s thrashing of Man Utd

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andoni Iraola believes it is too soon to consider Liverpool as potential Premier League title contenders after they thumped 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool were helped by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending-off for a last-man foul on Alexander Isak, with the Reds using their numerical advantage to ruthless effect.

Dominik Szoboszlai flashed home the free-kick from Yoro's challenge in the 10th minute before Florian Wirtz superbly turned Rio Ngumoha's cross into the net three minutes later.

Mauricio Pochettino, taking charge of United for the first time, introduced Harry Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo in an enforced change to try and bring some more defensive stability, but Liverpool eventually breached the Red Devils' back line in the second half.

Bradley Barcola's blistering run ended with a pinpoint cross for Ngumoha to tuck home, with Victor Munoz coming off the bench to seal an emphatic win eight minutes from time.

Since the start of the 2021-22 season, Liverpool's four wins by 4+ goals against United are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another in all competitions.

It was a result that moved Liverpool back into the top four and within one point of Manchester City and Brighton, who dropped points to Fulham and Hull City, respectively.

Arsenal are seven points clear of Liverpool after drawing 2-2 with Newcastle United, but Iraola was keen not to get carried away with the euphoria of beating the Reds' rivals.

"It's still early days. I think we are missing the two big games we lost here at home between Arsenal and [Man City]. They are making the difference in the standings," he said.

"This is still so early. This doesn't stop because we have a very difficult game against Club Brugge, and then we have the big derby."

4 – Since the start of the 2021-22 season, Liverpool's four wins by 4+ goals against Manchester United are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another. Another. https://t.co/c5BtjVXvlB

Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club.

Indeed, it was also the quickest Liverpool had gone 2-0 up in a Premier League match against United, going two ahead after just 12 minutes and 40 seconds.

Iraola is now unbeaten in his seven Premier League matches against United (W3 D4), and even quipped that his players could celebrate at half-time after going two goals in front.

"I think it's a big win; always against United it is a big game," Iraola added. "I think also you can enjoy it; you can see it coming.

"It's difficult to enjoy in the Premier League. Normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit and have lovely moments.

"We have missed some clear chances. In other games you will remember those chances; we've controlled the game, and everything was happening around the box.

"It's a 4-0 that was good for us in the standings but also confidence-wise, trying to get better results here at home."

There was also another standout display from Wirtz, who created 10 chances in open play for Liverpool, the most by a player in a Premier League match since Man City's David Silva against West Brom in March 2015 (11).

Wirtz now has eight goal involvements (three goals, five assists) in 16 appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, with the Liverpool attacker also starring in the international break under former Reds boss Jurgen Klopp with three goals in two games for Germany in the Nations League.

"He's in a lovely moment, and we want to keep him there as much as we can," Iraola said of Wirtz.

"He's in a situation against 10 players where you need players like him to control the situation and see the passes in behind.

"He's also arriving more and not just scoring but being a threat. He's becoming another option, and I'm happy with him."

Published: 14:09 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 18 November 2026

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’

BC.GAME, an online casino company, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Leicester City have axed a partnership with BC.GAME, after the gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador

Leicester confirmed fans who have purchased a replica shirt featuring the sponsor's name within the last 28 days can return it for a full refund or exchange by December 2

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too

In recent years, Leicester’s spectacular decline on the pitch has mirrored the relationship with their supporters.

During the years immediately before and after their stunning Premier League triumph in 2016, it was difficult to find a club more in tune with the fanbase.

But a series of baffling decisions – including the tie-up with BC.GAME – eroded trust between the club and their supporters.

Leicester are now in League One and face a long road back but sensible moves like this one suggest they are at least facing in the right direction again.

By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 11:18, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:35

Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki have both been left out of Manchester City’s starting lineup for this afternoon’s Premier League fixture against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.

Arbeloa has also opted to change his full-backs, with Kenny Tete and Ryan Sessegnon coming in for Timothy Castagne and Antonee Robinson. Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber retain their places at centre-back, though.
